votes.reason: «Internet fue temido como el fin de la capacidad de atención» follows the English passive in «The internet was once feared». «En su día se temía que internet acabara…» would sound more natural and make the past contrast clearer. This is a polish issue, not a factual loss.

«Recursos de clase mundial» conveys «world-class resources» and is understandable across regions. «De primer nivel» is a useful alternative, but the current wording does not create a readability defect.

The echo in «aparece un aparato nuevo y ya parece» makes the opening less sharp. The source moves directly from «emerges» to «civilization teeters»; removing «parece» would improve the rhythm and preserve that directness.

The candidate declares «sourceHash: "d5356a63e570"», which differs from the packet’s full source hash, but the checked packet does not define how this short field is calculated. Earlier supplied history carries the same declaration against the same source. The mismatch alone does not establish a failure; pipeline confirmation is reasonable, but it is not a demonstrated translation defect.

«Un mundo aumentado por la IA» closely tracks «an AI-augmented world», but «mundo aumentado» is abstract and can evoke augmented reality. A formulation such as «un mundo con la IA integrada» would keep the source’s broad relationship while making the recommendation easier to grasp; «como apoyo» would narrow it somewhat.

«Ganamos la capacidad de navegar con más frecuencia» preserves «gained the ability to navigate more often», yet feels heavy in a passage about finding one’s way through cities. «Ahora podemos orientarnos más a menudo» keeps the frequency claim and states the action directly. The source construction is also awkward, so this remains a modest readability issue.

As in issue f9ef93cb6eba1b8f5af3, «Internet fue temido como el fin de la capacidad de atención» is understandable but stiff. Recasting «The internet was once feared» as «En su día se temía que internet acabara…» retains the feared consequence and improves the Spanish rhythm.

«La IA seguirá seguramente este patrón» can read as probability where «AI will surely follow this pattern» sounds confidently predictive. The footnote supplies the caveat. A direct «La IA también seguirá este patrón» would better carry the main sentence’s confidence.

In «navegar con más frecuencia, en cualquier ciudad», the city and paper-map context points to «orientarnos». «Navegar» is intelligible in GPS usage, so calling it wholly wrong overstates the case; here the direct verb would read more naturally while retaining «navigate more often». This overlaps with issue ce4dca57c41eee60efdc.

«Los pánicos se repiten con tanta puntualidad» makes the setup for «poner en hora tu Apple Watch» work in Spanish. It loses some of the brevity of «set your Apple Watch by these panics», but gains a clear local joke without changing its point. Tightening it is optional.

«Ya parece que la civilización se tambalea» adds distance to «civilization teeters on the brink of idiocy». Removing «parece que» restores the source’s deadpan assertion and also fixes the sound echo noted in issue f158f4b3ee61d3f0c581.

«Hay niños de 12 años que no sabrían… pero pueden “escribir”» makes the source’s caricature more explicit, but «12-year-olds who couldn't… yet can “write”» already presents that group rhetorically. The shorter Spanish sentence gains readability without a material new claim.

«Repasemos el historial de estos pánicos» drops the slang flavor of «check our historical receipts», but it preserves the invitation to test the panic against history and fits the article’s direct voice. The stylistic loss is an acceptable adaptation.

«Muletas que dejarán coja a toda una generación» recreates the crutch and hobbling image in «crutches that will hobble a generation». «Toda una» gives the Spanish phrase idiomatic emphasis without materially changing its scope.
